generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, synthesis is what a literature review is built on. You do not report each study in turn; you make them speak to each other, noting where findings converge and where they conflict, and you build from them a position of your own. Converging evidence from several designs strengthens a claim; a failure to replicate complicates it. Drawing these together into your own argument, in the discipline's own terms, is synthesis.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students bring the same three studies to an essay.

Tom writes a paragraph on each study in turn: the first found this, the second argued that, the third reported something else. Each summary is accurate, and the three never meet. No claim of Tom's own emerges; the reader is left with three reports side by side. This is summary, not synthesis.

Amara makes the three studies speak to each other. Two converge on an effect, while the third, better controlled, fails to find it; Amara sets the convergence against the failed replication and argues, from the tension, that the effect is real but smaller and more fragile than first claimed. The studies become evidence for her own position. This is synthesis.

Both students used the same three studies. Only Amara drew them together into an argument of her own, which is what makes writing synthesis rather than summary.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, synthesis means drawing several studies together into an argument of your own, making them speak to each other rather than summarising each in turn, and expressing the result in the discipline's own vocabulary. You can now tell synthesis apart from summary and identify a synthesis move across sources. With analysis, evaluation and synthesis in hand, you can put the critical skills to work on purpose.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's writing synthesis rather than summary?

items.text: She set the studies against each other and built a claim of her own that none stated alone.
She wrote a separate, accurate paragraph on each study.
She used more studies than Tom did.
She quoted each study more fully.

feedback.correct: That's right. Making the studies speak to each other to build her own claim is synthesis.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara did ACROSS the studies, rather than reporting each one.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara synthesised: setting the studies against each other and building a claim none stated alone. Separate paragraphs, more studies or fuller quotes are still summary.
